propositions: _recall_false_accept computes specificity (true-negative rate, higher-is-better) but both consumption sites treat the result as a lower-is-better error rate, inverting the criterion.

The recorded frontier slot of the live Bedrock provider-parity run failed with 'false-accept rose 0.143' when the candidate was strictly more accurate (0.929 vs 0.786), penalizing fewer false fires instead of rewarding them.
The current computation `(not-blocked / safe)` is used against a ceiling of 0.10, making the gate effectively always-fail since any competent gate has specificity far above 0.10.

The fix corrects the computation to `(blocked / safe)` — the false-positive rate over safe items — matching the metric definition already established in eval.py and documented as lower-is-better in plan-review-gate.md.

The gold fixture in fidelity_spot_eval.py labelled must-block conflicts as 'advisory' (gold-safe), contradicting its own comments; relabelling to block-required reveals the false-accept lane from vacuous to real.
After the fix, the frontier false-accept failure clears (0.214→0.071 is a 14.3pp improvement, not regression), though the slot still fails on other criteria (agreement and decision flips).
